_README: Label id -> structure name for the anterolateral abdominal wall volume derived from the Visible Human male colour cryosections by scripts/cryo/abdominal_wall_from_cryo.py, plus the mapping onto atlas entities.

A KEY, not data. Rule-based: muscle-coloured voxels within 60 mm of the skin, anterior to the vertebral-body centre, in the trunk's own tissue component, not within 8 mm of any CT-labelled organ/bone and not the arms; rectus abdominis = within 70 mm of the midline and 70 mm behind the anterior midline skin; the lateral wall (>55 mm from the midline) split by depth fraction from the skin-facing boundary: external oblique (outer 40 %), internal oblique (middle 35 %), transversus abdominis (inner 25 %). From the xiphoid level to the bottom of the torso CT block (about the iliac crest), so the lowest part of the wall is missing. Volumes (r/l): rectus 225/226, external 195/350, internal 57/160, transversus 107/286 cm3 -- over-counted and left-right asymmetric; the layer boundaries are planes of depth fraction, not the real aponeurotic planes.
source: U.S. National Library of Medicine, The Visible Human Project (public domain), male colour cryosections, IDC series 4aaf9181-fb6a-4a4c-bf49-d1eb9ed4a385, registered to the CT (scripts/cryo/README.md). Rules from standard anatomy: Standring S (ed.), Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed., 'Anterior abdominal wall'.
